_note: Short reading versions of the D2 evaluation (22 Oct 2026), written from the cells and evaluation findings, matching report Table 7. Citations stay in 'Cell Evidence'.

Supervised assessment.verdict: The strongest check of what a student can do alone, but far from real practice and usually AI-free
Supervised assessment.strength: Verifies individual capability: in one module, viva and live-demo marks of about 35% and 44% sat behind take-home marks of 84%
Supervised assessment.weakness: Low realism and no place for AI use: time-limited conditions are far from professional practice

Unsupervised formats.verdict: Cheap and scalable, but weak on every validity criterion when AI is available
Unsupervised formats.strength: Scales to large cohorts at low cost, already run for 150 to over 750 students
Unsupervised formats.weakness: Marks say little about unaided ability: current GenAI completes most programming tasks, and markers cannot reliably spot AI work

Oral assessments.verdict: The best direct check of understanding; staff time is the main cost
Oral assessments.strength: Vivas exposed students who could not explain their own code, and live questioning is among the most AI-resistant checks
Oral assessments.weakness: Staff workload: at least 1,000 staff minutes per 100 students, and about 1,300 to 3,800 in practice

Practical demonstrations.verdict: A strong check of skills in real tools; staff time is the main cost
Practical demonstrations.strength: Live demos averaged 44% against 84% on take-home work, and checkoffs confirmed tool skills for 237 students
Practical demonstrations.weakness: Staff workload: checkoffs took about 80% of tutor office-hour time

Staged submissions.verdict: Makes the working process visible and lets AI use be sequenced, but each stage stays open to AI
Staged submissions.strength: Milestones show planning, drafts and AI use, so AI can be introduced in stages
Staged submissions.weakness: Each stage can still be completed with undisclosed AI help, and marking several stages adds workload

Process evidence.verdict: Useful when records are captured by the system and assessed by staff; student-kept logs verify little
Process evidence.strength: Code replay, repository history and graded interaction logs make AI use visible and assessable
Process evidence.weakness: Logs can be fabricated, and students' accounts did not match their AI traces, so a live check is still needed

Personalised tasks.verdict: Adds realism, but does not stop AI or show who did the work
Personalised tasks.strength: Realistic, personal contexts are widely recommended and make tasks more authentic
Personalised tasks.weakness: Personalising a task does not stop AI from completing it or show who did the work

AI-use declarations.verdict: Support transparency at low cost, but cannot show how AI was really used
AI-use declarations.strength: Support transparency and critical AI use at little cost
AI-use declarations.weakness: Self-reports did not match assessors' judgements, and undisclosed AI use is commonly 45% to 65%
